subject: Audit export: differential slices, retention windows, and integrity proofs
messages:
From: Helix Health Compliance <compliance@helixhealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: operator/admin activity slices and HMAC proofs for SOC2 sample

Hi Sergio,

We're starting work on the SOC 2 readiness window and need a clear, machine-readable export of admin/operator activity for our auditors. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide the following and estimate delivery lead time?

- Exact event types you log (we need to map to our control matrix): admin login, privilege grants/revokes, role changes, key/API token creations and revocations, config changes, console actions, operator-agent-run commands, session termination, and service-level automated failovers.
- For each event, which fields are included? (we prefer: event_id, timestamp (ISO+TZ), actor_id, actor_role, ip_address, user_agent, request_id, session_id, action, resource, pre_change, post_change, geo, tenant_id)
- Sampling vs full export options: can we request full-day snapshots, delta/differential slices (start/end window), or a bounded-consistent sampling?
- Retention guarantees: how long are live admin events retained vs archived? If archived, what's the retrieval SLA and format?
- Evidence integrity: can you provide an HMAC-signed manifest per export and checksums for each file (SHA256)? Will Redwood sign an attestation for chain-of-custody?
- Delivery: supported transport methods (S3 presigned, SFTP, HTTPS push) and acceptable formats (JSONL, Parquet, gzipped CSV).
- PII/redaction: if events include email addresses or user PII, we need to know whether Redwood redacts, tokenizes, or includes mapping tables (and where mapping is stored).

We'd like a short sample export (up to 24 hours) to validate schema before the audit. Target turnaround is 5 business days. Please cc internal compliance contact Jeremy (jeremy@bluecare-audits.com) on replies.

Thanks,
Anna Morales
Head of Compliance, Helix Health
compliance@helixhealth.com

Attachments: none
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Helix Health Compliance <compliance@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 09:45:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: operator/admin activity slices and HMAC proofs for SOC2 sample

Hi Anna / Jeremy,

Thanks for the clear list — we can accommodate all of that. High-level answers and next steps below; I can pull a schema + sample export and a signed manifest once you confirm the preferred delivery path.

What we log (canonical):
- auth.login (success/fail), auth.token.create, auth.token.revoke, admin.role.update, admin.user.create, admin.user.delete, admin.privilege.grant, admin.privilege.revoke, config.change, console.exec, operator.action, session.start, session.end, system.failover, key.rotate

Per-event fields we include (exportable):
- event_id, occurred_at (ISO 8601 UTC), timezone_hint (client tz if available), actor_id, actor_internal_id (if Redwood user), actor_role, tenant_id, request_id, session_id, source_ip, user_agent, action, resource_path, change_before, change_after, trace_id, region, node_id, retention_tier

Export modes supported:
- Full snapshot (time-bounded): JSONL / Parquet gzipped; includes all fields.
- Differential (delta) slices: we can export changed-events between two timestamps; suitable for incremental handoffs.
- Continuous stream: S3 streaming endpoint with rolling manifests (for long-running evidence pipelines).
- Sampling: we do not recommend sampling for SOC 2 evidentiary pulls, but we can produce deterministic sampled subsets by request.

Retention / archive:
- Live (hot) indexed admin events: 90 days by default (configurable on Dedicated/Private plans).
- Warm archive: 1 year (fast retrieval within 48 hours).
- Cold archive: immutable snapshots stored 7+ years (retrieval SLA differs; typically 5 business days and requires an attested request).

Integrity & chain of custody:
- Each export is accompanied by a manifest.jsonl describing files, record counts, row-level checksums (SHA256), and an HMAC-SHA256 over the manifest using a Redwood export key.
- We can additionally sign the manifest with a Redwood corporate PGP key on request for legal attestation.
- We include per-file checksums in a separate checksums.txt (attached sample).

Delivery options (we support):
- S3 presigned PUT (preferred for large exports), s3:// or presigned-get/push
- Managed SFTP to customer-hosted endpoint
- HTTPS push (mutual TLS) to a customer ingestion endpoint

PII handling:
- By default, events contain identifiable fields for troubleshooting. For SOC 2 exports we offer two redaction policies: 1) pseudonymize (replace PII with stable tokens) with token mapping retained in your tenant vault (not exported), or 2) redact inline (PII fields replaced with <REDACTED>) and noted in manifest. We will not export mapping tables unless explicitly requested and covered in an NDA/attestation.

Attachments: I attached a small sample manifest and an export sample CSV to illustrate field layout (audit_manifest_v1.jsonl, export_sample_manifest.csv) and a checksums file (hmac_checksums.txt).

If that looks good, please confirm: (a) time window you want for the sample, (b) delivery method, and (c) whether you want pseudonymization or redaction. I can turn around the sample within 48 hours once those are confirmed.

Sergio
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: audit_manifest_v1.jsonl (sample), export_sample_manifest.csv (sample), hmac_checksums.txt (sample)
From: Helix Health Compliance <compliance@helixhealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Jeremy Lowe <jeremy@bluecare-audits.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 11:02:07 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: operator/admin activity slices and HMAC proofs for SOC2 sample

Hi Sergio,

Appreciate the detailed rundown — that covers most of our checklist. A few clarifications before you prepare the sample export:

1) Time window: please produce a delta export covering 2028-01-01T00:00:00Z through 2028-01-17T23:59:59Z. That lets our auditors validate both snapshot completeness and rollover semantics.
2) Retention guarantee statement: we need a written note stating default live retention (90 days) and the retrieval SLA for warm (48 hours) and cold (5 business days) archives — we will include that in our SOC 2 evidence binder.
3) Manifest contents: confirm manifest includes per-file SHA256, record counts, first_event_ts, last_event_ts, tenant_id, and a manifest_hmac computed over manifest.jsonl (HMAC-SHA256). We will verify the HMAC using the public key or a shared secret.
4) Pseudonymization: for this sample please pseudonymize user-identifiable fields and do not include mapping tables. We will request mapping in a separate legal flow only if strictly necessary.

Delivery: S3 presigned URL is preferred. Turnaround: target is 5 business days — please notify if you need more time.

Also: will Redwood provide a short attestation letter (PDF) that the exported data is a true copy of the product's admin activity for the requested window and that the HMAC/checksum process was applied? Our auditors require that in case of third-party validation.

Thanks,
Anna

On behalf of Helix Health Compliance Team
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helix Health Compliance <compliance@helixhealth.com>, Jeremy Lowe <jeremy@bluecare-audits.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 15:38:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: operator/admin activity slices and HMAC proofs for SOC2 sample

Team — forwarding the thread and next steps. Action items:

- Kimberly: please schedule the delta export job for 2028-01-01T00:00:00Z -> 2028-01-17T23:59:59Z; output format compressed JSONL + manifest.jsonl. Set manifest fields to include: file_name, sha256_hex, record_count, first_event_ts, last_event_ts, tenant_id, region.
- Hannah: generate the HMAC over manifest.jsonl using the export-key for this tenant; produce hmac_checksums.txt and sign the attestation PDF with legal. We'll use HMAC-SHA256 and provide the verification instructions to Helix.
- Karthik: coordinate S3 presigned PUT endpoint and notify Helix with credentials/links; set ACL to private and rotation TTL to 72 hours. Also confirm pseudonymization transform pipeline (stable tokenization) has been applied in the export.

We will aim for delivery within 5 business days. I attached the sample manifest and checksums to the previous reply for reference.
